theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem robust_tank_step (x y u w cap sensor inflow : ℝ)
    (hmeasurement : |x-y| ≤ sensor) (hdisturbance : |w| ≤ inflow)
    (hlower : sensor+inflow-y ≤ u)
    (hupper : u ≤ cap-sensor-inflow-y) :
    x+u+w ∈ Icc 0 cap
theorems.scope: Universal interval implication for x+u+w: bounded measurement error and inflow plus both action endpoints imply next volume in [0,cap].
limitations: The affine sampled update and deterministic error bounds are hypotheses; actuator feasibility and intersample safety are separate.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tank_original_step (x y u w : ℝ)
    (hmeasurement : |x-y| ≤ 1/10) (hdisturbance : |w| ≤ 1/5)
    (hinput : u ∈ Icc (3/10-y) (97/10-y)) :
    x+u+w ∈ Icc 0 10
theorems.scope: Exact specialization sensor=1/10, inflow=1/5, cap=10, action interval [3/10-y,97/10-y].
limitations: One update only; the actuator interval is not needed for this implication.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tank_filter_feasible (y : ℝ) (hy : y ∈ Icc (-1/10) (101/10)) :
    ∃ u : ℝ, u ∈ Icc (-1) 1 ∧ u ∈ Icc (3/10-y) (97/10-y)
theorems.scope: For every valid measurement y in [-1/10,101/10], constructs an input satisfying both [-1,1] actuator and sufficient safety intervals.
limitations: Does not optimize distance to the learned nominal command.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tank_measurement_feedback (y : ℝ) (hy : y ∈ Icc (-1/10) (101/10)) :
    ∃ u : ℝ, u ∈ Icc (-1) 1 ∧
      ∀ x w : ℝ, |x-y| ≤ 1/10 → |w| ≤ 1/5 → x+u+w ∈ Icc 0 10
theorems.scope: For each valid measured y there exists an actuator-bounded u which succeeds for every compatible real state x and every bounded inflow w.
limitations: Verifies the action-before-state-uncertainty quantifier order; no state-estimation probability or hardware model identification is encoded.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tank_sampled_invariance (x y u w : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hzero : x 0 ∈ Icc 0 10)
    (hmeasurement : ∀ n, |x n-y n| ≤ 1/10)
    (hdisturbance : ∀ n, |w n| ≤ 1/5)
    (hinput : ∀ n, u n ∈ Icc (3/10-y n) (97/10-y n))
    (hupdate : ∀ n, x (n+1) = x n+u n+w n) :
    ∀ n, x n ∈ Icc 0 10
theorems.scope: All natural-number sample states satisfy [0,10] if the initial state, per-step measurements, disturbances, selected input certificates, and update equalities hold.
limitations: Input certificates at all times are hypotheses here; recursive applicability is established separately.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tank_feedback_recursive_invariance (x y w : ℕ → ℝ) (policy : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hzero : x 0 ∈ Icc 0 10)
    (hmeasurement : ∀ n, |x n-y n| ≤ 1/10)
    (hdisturbance : ∀ n, |w n| ≤ 1/5)
    (hpolicy : ∀ measured ∈ Icc (-1/10 : ℝ) (101/10),
      policy measured ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1 ∧
      policy measured ∈ Icc (3/10-measured) (97/10-measured))
    (hupdate : ∀ n, x (n+1) = x n+policy (y n)+w n) :
    ∀ n, x n ∈ Icc 0 10
theorems.scope: Induction proves sampled invariance for a fixed feedback satisfying the safety/actuator intervals on valid measurements. Current safety implies next measurement remains in the feedback applicability domain.
limitations: Requires exact sampled dynamics and bounded sensor/inflow sequences; no assumptions about independence and no intersample volume claim.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tank_no_shared_input :
    ¬ ∃ u : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 10,
      ∀ w ∈ Icc (-1/5 : ℝ) (1/5), x+u+w ∈ Icc 0 10
theorems.scope: No single constant input can protect all x in [0,10] from every inflow in [-1/5,1/5].
limitations: This negation does not preclude measurement-dependent feedback.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tank_large_disturbance_impossible (u : ℝ) (hu : u ≤ 1) :
    ¬ (0+u-6/5 ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 10)
theorems.scope: At true state zero and inflow -6/5, any input at most 1 produces a negative next volume.
limitations: Formalizes physical impossibility with exact current state; it does not encode the alternative wider measurement-interval certificate.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem policy_mix_feasible (p : ℝ) :
    (p ∈ Icc 0 1 ∧ mixCost p ≤ 1) ↔ p ∈ Icc 0 (4/9)
theorems.scope: For every real p, probability bounds plus mixCost(p)<=1 are equivalent to p in [0,4/9].
limitations: mixCost is the stipulated one-state discounted summary; its derivation from a stochastic process is not encoded.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem policy_mix_constrained_optimum (p : ℝ) (_hp : p ∈ Icc 0 1)
    (hc : mixCost p ≤ 1) : mixReward p ≤ 100/3
theorems.scope: Every feasible p in [0,1] has mixReward(p)<=100/3.
limitations: Universal bound over this one-dimensional policy family, rather than arbitrary MDP policies.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem policy_mix_unique_optimum (p : ℝ) :
    mixReward p = 100/3 ↔ p = 4/9
theorems.scope: Reward equals 100/3 exactly when p=4/9.
limitations: Feasibility/attainment are separate declarations.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem policy_mix_optimum_attained :
    (4/9 : ℝ) ∈ Icc 0 1 ∧ mixCost (4/9) = 1 ∧ mixReward (4/9) = 100/3
theorems.scope: The exact p=4/9 is a probability, attains cost 1, and attains reward 100/3.
limitations: No trajectory-level safety conclusion follows from expected cost.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem policy_mix_budget_optimum (budget : ℝ)
    (hb : budget ∈ Icc (1/5 : ℝ) 2) :
    (5*budget-1)/9 ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧
      mixCost ((5*budget-1)/9) = budget ∧
      ∀ p : ℝ, mixCost p ≤ budget →
        mixReward p ≤ mixReward ((5*budget-1)/9)
theorems.scope: For any budget in [1/5,2], p*=(5*budget-1)/9 is a probability, attains that cost, and upper-bounds the reward of every policy with cost<=budget.
limitations: Covers the fixed discount 9/10; the changed-discount B2 model is not formalized here.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem policy_mix_flat_lagrangian (p : ℝ) :
    mixReward p-(50/3)*(mixCost p-1) = 100/3
theorems.scope: At multiplier 50/3 and budget 1, the reward Lagrangian is identically 100/3 for every real p.
limitations: Flatness of the inner objective alone does not identify a unique policy or formalize a global dual minimization theorem.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem held_barrier_affine (initial slope horizon t : ℝ)
    (hinitial : 0 ≤ initial) (ht : t ∈ Icc 0 horizon)
    (hterminal : 0 ≤ initial+slope*horizon) :
    0 ≤ initial+slope*t
theorems.scope: For every t between zero and a horizon, an affine lower trajectory is nonnegative if its initial and terminal values are nonnegative.
limitations: Order-theoretic all-times statement; no differential equation or integration theorem is encoded.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem held_barrier_clearance (clearance : ℝ → ℝ)
    (initial input disturbance horizon : ℝ) (hinitial : 0 ≤ initial)
    (hterminal : 0 ≤ initial+(input-disturbance)*horizon)
    (hlower : ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) horizon,
      initial+(input-disturbance)*t ≤ clearance t) :
    ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) horizon, 0 ≤ clearance t
theorems.scope: A real-time clearance function is nonnegative throughout the hold if it dominates the affine initial-plus-worst-slope line and the line has safe endpoints.
limitations: The line lower bound is an explicit hypothesis. Its derivation from integrating bounded physical velocity and the numerical noisy/delayed input choices are not formalized.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem held_barrier_half_second (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) (1/2)) :
    0 ≤ 3/10+(-1/2-1/10)*t
theorems.scope: At the chapter constants initial 3/10 and slope -3/5, the lower bound is nonnegative at every real t in [0,1/2].
limitations: Verifies the held-command lower line, conditional on the model-to-line argument.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem held_barrier_late_counterexample :
    (3/10 : ℝ)+(-1/2-1/10)*1 = -3/10 ∧ (-3/10 : ℝ) < 0
theorems.scope: Holding the same command to t=1 gives lower line -3/10<0.
limitations: A negative lower bound alone is not an actual violation; the prose supplies a constant worst-disturbance trajectory attaining it. That trajectory integration is not encoded.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tube_invariant_step (x q error radius allowance : ℝ)
    (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hx : |x| ≤ radius) (he : |error| ≤ allowance)
    (hbudget : q*radius+allowance ≤ radius) :
    |q*x+error| ≤ radius
theorems.scope: For any nonnegative scalar q, |x|<=radius and |error|<=allowance imply |q*x+error|<=radius when q*radius+allowance<=radius.
limitations: The uniform error bound and applicability domain are hypotheses; no learned approximation training guarantee is proved.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tube_sampled_invariance (x error : ℕ → ℝ) (q radius allowance : ℝ)
    (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hzero : |x 0| ≤ radius)
    (he : ∀ n, |error n| ≤ allowance)
    (hbudget : q*radius+allowance ≤ radius)
    (hupdate : ∀ n, x (n+1) = q*x n+error n) :
    ∀ n, |x n| ≤ radius
theorems.scope: For arbitrary natural-number bounded error sequences and an affine scalar recursion, the radius condition implies all sample states remain in the tube.
limitations: No continuous-time trajectory or asymptotic convergence claim.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tube_thermal_errors (w approximation : ℝ)
    (hw : |w| ≤ 1/20) (ha : |approximation| ≤ 1/50) :
    |w+approximation| ≤ 7/100
theorems.scope: Disturbance magnitude <=1/20 and controller approximation magnitude <=1/50 imply combined error magnitude <=7/100.
limitations: Deterministic pointwise assumptions; no statistical validation or mean-square-error conversion.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tube_thermal_radius (x error : ℝ)
    (hx : |x| ≤ 7/50) (he : |error| ≤ 7/100) :
    |(1/2)*x+error| ≤ 7/50
theorems.scope: The scalar closed map with coefficient 1/2 preserves |x|<=7/50 under every error of magnitude <=7/100.
limitations: A sufficient deviation tube, not an identified physical model.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem tube_error_envelope (x : ℕ → ℝ) (q allowance : ℝ)
    (hq₀ : 0 ≤ q) (hq₁ : q < 1)
    (hstep : ∀ n, |x (n+1)| ≤ q*|x n|+allowance) :
    ∀ n, |x n| ≤ allowance/(1-q)+q^n*(|x 0|-allowance/(1-q))
theorems.scope: For every n, a magnitude recurrence with 0<=q<1 obeys allowance/(1-q)+q^n*(|x0|-allowance/(1-q)).
limitations: Proves the universal finite-time envelope. The limit and convergence-in-probability claims are not encoded; application interprets allowance as nonnegative.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem lipschitz_observation_transfer {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    (f : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (hf : LipschitzWith L f)
    (x z : X) (observation error radius : ℝ)
    (ho : |observation-f z| ≤ error) (hr : dist x z ≤ radius) :
    observation-error-L*radius ≤ f x
theorems.scope: For every point of any pseudometric domain, a deterministic bounded observation error and a true LipschitzWith bound imply the reading-minus-error-minus-distance-cost lower bound.
limitations: Lipschitz regularity and error envelope are hypotheses; no GP/RKHS or adaptive-noise theorem is encoded.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem lipschitz_ball_safety {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    (f : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (hf : LipschitzWith L f)
    (z : X) (observation error radius threshold : ℝ)
    (ho : |observation-f z| ≤ error)
    (hmargin : threshold ≤ observation-error-L*radius) :
    ∀ x ∈ Metric.closedBall z radius, threshold ≤ f x
theorems.scope: Every point in a closed metric ball satisfies a threshold if its observed lower margin pays for L times the ball radius.
limitations: No positive-L division is used, so L=0 is included. Safety of a complete experiment still depends on the definition of its margin function.

theorems.exact_formal_statement:
theorem lipschitz_implemented_parameter {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    (f : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (hf : LipschitzWith L f)
    (actual command observed : X) (value error displacement realization threshold : ℝ)
    (ho : |value-f observed| ≤ error)
    (hcommand : dist command observed ≤ displacement)
    (hrealization : dist actual command ≤ realization)
    (hmargin : threshold ≤ value-error-L*(displacement+realization)) :
    threshold ≤ f actual
theorems.scope: If the command is within displacement of an observed parameter and realization is within another bound of the command, a margin paying L times their sum certifies the actual implemented parameter.
limitations: Sufficient triangle-inequality certificate. Does not prove the exact erosion of a union of intervals in B1 or multi-constraint numerical endpoints in B2.
